business_problem: IBM's Chief Data Office needed a better way to monitor and troubleshoot thousands of data pipelines because manual health checks and report creation were time-consuming, error-prone, and threatened trust in the timeliness and quality of shared enterprise data.
solution_summary: The IBM Chief Data Office adopted IBM watsonx.data integration as a unified control plane for continuous data observability across nearly 4,000 pipelines. The team began with a pilot on merger-and-acquisition data, using real-time monitoring, custom alerts, automated workflows, dashboards, and directed acyclic graph views to track pipeline health and identify bottlenecks quickly. After proving the approach, the CDO expanded the capability into a single source of truth for pipeline performance across the organization. Engineers can now review historical run trends, inspect run status, identify root causes, and generate health reports from the same environment instead of assembling those insights manually from multiple products. That shared observability layer frees engineering capacity for new data integration work and shifts the operating model from reactive troubleshooting toward proactive data-quality management.

solution_components.name: IBM watsonx.data integration
solution_components.role: Continuously monitors pipeline health, triggers alerts, and provides dashboards and DAG views for data observability.

data_flow: Pipeline run data, health indicators, and failure events from thousands of enterprise data pipelines are collected into watsonx.data integration, where alerts, dashboards, historical trends, and DAG views help engineers spot issues and resolve them before downstream users are affected.
business_outcome: The CDO reduced the engineering effort required for monitoring and reporting, became more proactive about pipeline health, and improved the experience for teams that rely on accurate, timely enterprise data.
